previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction, and autonomic neuropathy was admitted for symptomatic hypotension after a dialysis session. Initial blood pressure was 74/45 mmHg, which improved with a 500 mL saline bolus. The hypotension was attributed to hypovolemia from excessive fluid removal during dialysis. Her dialysis regimen was adjusted to limit fluid removal and maintain a slightly higher volume status. A chest X-ray showed new right and worsening left pleural effusions with atelectasis, possibly infectious, prompting a short course of levofloxacin. Her TSH was elevated at 26, leading to an increase in levothyroxine from 150 to 175 mcg daily. She was also treated for vaginal discharge with metronidazole and started on potassium supplementation for hypokalemia. She remained stable, was discharged to extended care, and will follow up with nephrology, cardiology, podiatry, and hand clinic.
